title: Which pages should an editor review first? A time-aware, site-relative decline-risk queue for content refresh
abstract: Which visible pages should a content editor review first, before they lose search visibility? Using the FlyRank pseudonymized warehouse release (78,835,655 daily rows, 27 Jan 2025 to 30 Jun 2026), we built a monthly page panel and labelled a page as declining when its next-month daily impressions fell more than 20% below the median page of its own site, so that site-wide shocks are not mistaken for page decay. A histogram gradient-boosting model using only information available at the decision date was selected on May 2026 and evaluated once on a sealed June 2026 month (89,237 pages, base rate 39.6%), reaching PR-AUC 0.724 versus 0.683 for the best transparent momentum rule (gap +0.041, 95% client-bootstrap CI +0.021 to +0.067), while an impact-ordered version of the score covers 66% of site-relative lost impressions in its top 10% of pages. The output is a ranked, reason-coded review queue for decision support; it does not show that refreshing a page causes recovery.
introduction: Editors have limited review hours; ~90k visible pages per month need triage. The decision supported: which pages enter next month's review queue, with what action and why.
key_findings: Absolute decline label swings from 5% to 79% with site-wide shocks; the site-relative label is stable at 31–40%.
Sealed test: model PR-AUC 0.724 / ROC-AUC 0.800 vs B2 rule 0.683 / 0.755.
On unseen clients the gap over B2 shrinks to +0.013 PR-AUC.
The w04 volume rule ranks worse than chance for site-relative decline (ROC-AUC 0.38) but finds high-stake pages.
Score drivers are momentum signals (page vs. site trend, late-month slide) — observed associations, not ranking factors.
Queue back-test: PROTECT pages (5% of pages) held 41% of site-relative lost impressions.
acknowledgment: Built on the FlyRank ML Internship dataset (https://flyrank.ai).
